previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted following a syncopal episode at home, resulting in a fall and head strike. Initial CT showed a small subarachnoid hemorrhage, which resolved on repeat imaging the next day. Syncope was attributed to likely vasovagal or hypotensive causes, possibly exacerbated by recent increases in isosorbide mononitrate and transition to extended-release metoprolol, along with poor oral intake and a urinary tract infection. He was found to have a catheter-related MRSA infection, requiring IV vancomycin via a PICC line. The Imdur dose was reduced from 90 mg to 60 mg daily due to hypotensive concerns. He was cleared by physical therapy, remained neurologically stable, and was discharged to an extended care facility for completion of antibiotic therapy. Outpatient follow-up was arranged for meningioma monitoring, renal mass surveillance, and primary care coordination.

___ with history of CAD, diet controlled diabetes, recent

malaise and abdominal pain, found to have copious WBC on UA.

colonization in the setting of chronic indwelling Foley and 
dystonic bladder rather than a new UTI.  This is supported by

felt strongly that he should not be treated for active UTI 
unless there was presence of concomitant sepsis.  Had Foley 
changed overnight.  He received one dose of meropenum and 
vancomycin overnight, but further antibiotics were not given.

use this for 3 days.  Encouraged PO hydration.  Contacted his 
outpt providers including Dr. ___ and Dr. ___

prevent development of resistance.  Long discussion was had and 
patient was educated on chronic colonization and the reasoning 
behind not treating with antibiotics at this point.  He was 
instructed to present to his PCP or ___ should he develop fever, 
lightheadedness, confusion, pyruria or hematuria.
